records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the

condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: L4 Caco-2 records for polar ribonucleoside/cytidine analogs show low permeability: levovirin 0.12×10^-6 cm/s (C50) and gemcitabine <1×10^-6 / 0.99×10^-6 cm/s (C52, C58), supporting poor passive absorption for the highly polar query.

L5 bidirectional transport records show low A→B permeability and efflux for nucleoside analogs: EFdA A→B ~4-6×10^-7 cm/s (C60, C64), GS-441524 A→B 0.229×10^-6 cm/s with BCRP/MDR1 efflux (C62, C65, C67, C70), and cladribine BCRP-mediated efflux (C59, C68, C69), indicating gut-wall efflux as a plausible presystemic loss mechanism.

L1 gold outcomes for other nucleoside scaffolds are mixed: emtricitabine 92% (C16, C33) and didanosine 38% (C13, C32) show some nucleosides reach F≥20%, but acyclovir is at 20% (C06); these scaffolds differ from the ribonucleoside query and do not affirmatively establish F≥20% for 5-azacytidine.

L6 hepatic clearance records for other nucleosides (GS-441524 not a CYP substrate, C78/C80; zidovudine low UGT intrinsic clearance, C71-C77/C79/C82) do not measure the query's cytidine deaminase pathway and are of low transferability; they do not provide affirmative evidence for F<20% or F≥20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for 5-azacytidine is present in the supplied records.
No query-specific Caco-2/MDCK permeability, efflux, or intestinal metabolism data; all L4/L5 records are for analog nucleosides with inferred transferability.
Cytidine deaminase-mediated first-pass metabolism and gut-wall metabolism for the query are not directly measured; L6 records cover CYP and UGT pathways only.
Possible CNT/ENT transporter-mediated uptake for the query is not directly measured; L5 substrate records for gemcitabine/NHC are analog evidence only.
The query_prior reasoning text names guanosine, but the canonical SMILES corresponds to 5-azacytidine; the prior is treated only as an uncertain physicochemical prior.
High-F records for emtricitabine/didanosine come from different nucleoside scaffolds; their transferability to the ribonucleoside query is limited.
content.decision_summary: Prediction remains low with moderate confidence.
